input.quote: Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: The Agreement has no indemnification clause anywhere: there is no Section 20, and no defend/hold-harmless/indemnify obligation on either Party. Several provisions nonetheless assume an indemnity exists — Section 9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5" (a dangling reference), Section 19.4 preserves remedies for "indemnified claims", Section 21.3 treats "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims, and Section 30.5 protects "an indemnified party" and "vested indemnity rights". With no Vendor IP indemnity at all this sits in walk-away territory, so we have inserted a new Section 20 at the preferred position (Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data breach, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice/control/cooperation procedure) and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. We did not adopt the fallback super-cap of 3× annual fees because Section 21.3 already carves indemnification obligations out of the liability cap and importing a super-cap would reduce our existing protection.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 20 (Indemnification): Vendor defence and indemnity for IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data breach, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; claim procedure; narrow Customer indemnity.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity at all, even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one exists, so we have inserted a new Section 20 requiring Vendor to defend and indemnify us and our Affiliates for third-party IP claims, its breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data breaches, and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and our own indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend and indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses, to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, the indemnifying Party shall control the defence and settlement of the claim, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation.
Customer shall indemnify Vendor against third-party claims to the extent arising out of content Customer provides for use in the Services or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

mappings.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
